chunks.content: etcd supports TLS and certificate authentication for client and peer traffic. Use a separately signed key pair for each member, and put every address clients actually use in that member certificate's subject alternative names. An address mismatch must fail closed; changing the endpoint to an unverified name is not a repair.

A three-member etcd cluster tolerates one member failure and needs two voting members to commit changes. Member-list output proves membership, while endpoint health proves the members can commit a proposal; neither check alone proves the entire DCS contract.

Streaming replication sends WAL records as they are generated. It is asynchronous by default, so a commit can precede replay on a standby. The primary needs replication authentication and enough WAL senders and slots; a healthy result shows one sender/receiver pair in streaming state for each attached replica.

Data checksums protect database pages and are enabled for the whole cluster during initdb or during an offline operation. Checksums also satisfy one pg_rewind prerequisite. They do not replace backups, WAL retention, full_page_writes, or a tested restore procedure.

Patroni writes bootstrap.dcs into the DCS only when it initializes a new cluster. Editing bootstrap.dcs in local YAML after initialization does not change the running cluster; use patronictl edit-config or the REST API for later dynamic configuration changes.

Patroni role-health endpoints distinguish the primary from replicas. A writer router must check the primary-specific endpoint rather than accepting any open PostgreSQL port, because a healthy replica must not receive writes.

HAProxy active checks remove a server after the configured consecutive failure threshold and restore it after the configured consecutive success threshold. An HTTP check can connect to Patroni's REST port, send GET /primary, and require status 200 while forwarding PostgreSQL TCP traffic on port 5432.

A planned switchover identifies the current leader and an eligible candidate, checks cluster health, changes leadership through Patroni, and then proves the application path. It is different from failover because the old leader is expected to cooperate.

pg_rewind synchronizes a former primary whose timeline diverged from the new primary. It requires data checksums or wal_log_hints and full_page_writes, and may require recovery configuration correction afterward. Rewind is not a substitute for fencing the old writer first.

Mattermost needs a dedicated operating-system account, writable data location, PostgreSQL data source, and supervised service. Startup readiness must include its system ping and database migrations through the stable HAProxy endpoint; database process health alone does not prove the application path.
